text:
Valeri Nichushkin's first season in Columbus hasn't gone the way either side hoped. A Stanley Cup winner in Colorado in 2022, he has two goals and 10 points in 19 games, and one goal in his last ten while the Blue Jackets lost seven of them.

The concern isn't luck. His own chances are down sharply: 0.47 expected goals per 60, against 1.07 last season in Denver, and the Blue Jackets have been outchanced with him on (47% of the expected goals at five on five). Some of that is context. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.1 wins last season, a real two-way driver, but also noted he played with some of the best teammates in the league, which made everything easier.

His minutes are going up, not down: 18:20 over the last ten, and with Sean Monahan out, Dmitri Voronkov has moved onto his line. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a clean puck-mover last season, carrying in and out with possession. Columbus needs that version, and the chances to come with it.
